incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service=infer-gpu-nodes severity=critical host=giant-gpu-12 zone=us-west-2a metric=kubelet_not_ready :rotating_light:

pagerduty: New incident PD-2026-8743 created. Escalation policy: oncall -> sre-amber -> infra-liz. Links: https://pd.example/PD-2026-8743

oncall-tomas: acked in PD. I'm taking primary. pinging @sre-amber and @infra-liz. :wave:

sre-amber: I'm online. pulling logs from cluster 'infer-prod-2'. Can someone confirm if dedicated customer pools are impacted?

eng-runtime-raj: seeing 5xx surge on /v1/stream and increased retries to fallback models since ~1785009700. Route traffic shifted to fallback model group (bg-gpu) for ~40% of requests.

customer-success-olivia: notified two dedicated customers on the affected pools via the incident template. response: "we're seeing increased latency" from acct-zenith.

infra-liz: node 'giant-gpu-12' unreachable over ssh. serial console shows kernel oops followed by soft lockup. Attempting forced reboot via provider API now.

oncall-tomas: any evidence of kubelet crashloops or pods stuck?

sre-amber: kubelet logs show repeated segfaults before node lost heartbeat. snippet:
```
Mar 21 12:35:01 giant-gpu-12 kubelet[1234]: runtime: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
Mar 21 12:35:01 giant-gpu-12 kubelet[1234]: goroutine 58 [running]:
Mar 21 12:35:01 giant-gpu-12 kubelet[1234]: panic: runtime error:
```

infra-liz: serial snippet (truncated):
```
[    7.345678] kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000020
[    7.345682] RIP: 0010:[<ffffffff81d2345a>] gpu_driver_fault+0x7a/0x120
[    7.345686] Code: Bad RIP value
```

sre-amber: looks like GPU driver/kernel panic. I'll cordon and drain to protect other nodes: `kubectl cordon giant-gpu-12` then `kubectl drain giant-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` executed. Pods are getting rescheduled.

eng-runtime-raj: applied temporary routing policy to prefer us-west-2b and small-gpu variants to reduce tail latencies. config change pushed (no downtime).

oncall-tomas: confirmed: about 18 pods were rescheduled from that node; retry queues cleared for most customers. still watching errors in service mesh for older connections.

pagerduty: User 'oncall-tomas' acknowledged incident at 1785010100.

infra-liz: reboot via provider failed with timeout; hardware team ticket opened (HT-8892). serial shows repeated ECC errors prior to oops. marking node for replacement.

sre-amber: mitigation summary: cordoned node, drained, applied routing fallback, notified affected customers, hardware replacement in progress. Observability: error rate dropped from 22% to 2% in 12 minutes; tail p99 latency returning to baseline.

oncall-tomas: planning next steps: if node replacement completes, we'll reimage and run soak tests before returning to pool. leaving notes in PD and the cluster runbook. Handoff to night oncall @sre-nina in 25m.

sre-nina: will take watch. acked and monitoring dashboards. please leave escalation notes if hardware team needs follow-up. :thumbsup:

customer-success-olivia: updated customers with ETA for replacement and confirmed they have fallbacks active.

sre-amber: monitoring for 30m. will escalate if any regression. adding alert to watch for kubelet segfault pattern across other nodes.

incident-bot: PD-2026-8743 marked resolved by user 'sre-amber' at 1785010800. Incident closed.

oncall-tomas: thanks team — good run. closing thread after postmortem if needed. :white_check_mark:
